articleTitle: Clustering Technique for Enhanced Optimization and Control of Distribution Networks
abstract: Significant changes in the structure and nature of consumption in distribution networks are causing significant challenges for distribution network operators. To maintain a high level of reliability and security of supply, the operation of a low-voltage network in the near future has to be supported by sophisticated optimization and control algorithms. However, the low voltage network is a challenging environment, involving a large number of different network participants. The large number of controlled entities makes the optimization and control of this type of network a difficult task. To decrease the complexity of the problem, a clustering technique is presented. The proposed clustering technique allows aggregation of individual network participants into several groups (clusters), that can be controlled as a single entity while respecting the impacts of individual network participants on the network operation. The presented clustering technique is demonstrated on a sample network based on a real low-voltage feeder.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Safety Functions for the CNC Milling Machine
abstract: The paper deals with the design and implementation of safety functions for a CNC milling machine. It is a relatively small CNC milling machine that does not pose a great danger to trained persons. Because it is used in areas where even untrained persons can come into contact with it, it was necessary to implement a safety system that implements safety functions preventing accidents when entering the dangerous zone of the CNC milling machine. The safety system is implemented based on a safety PLC and the sensors are designed using a two-channel architecture to meet the required SIL (safety integrity level).

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage System as a Power Supply for a Defined Power Profile
abstract: In this paper, the focus is given on the current control from the supercapacitor for peak power and accumulator for continuous power delivery required during operation. The practical application of this paper is a power supply for the electric drive of the robotic arm. The accumulator and supercapacitor storage system's control algorithm is shown. The supercapacitor is linked in parallel to the common node via the bidirectional converter, while the accumulator is directly connected to the load. With an uncontrolled DC voltage and a current-controlled source, the peak power demand is subsequently simulated. The used bidirectional converter operates in the current mode and does not need the voltage controller. The benefit of the control method is that it just uses the load current measurement, rather than requiring information regarding load demand from the robotic system.

articleTitle: Overview of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Topologies in E-mobility Applications
abstract: This research summarizes the current state of the art of power electronics used in E-mobility dynamic wireless power charging. The paper introduces power electronics topology and topologies of the power input part including drive and switching strategies. It also introduces the technical outlook for the future and follow-up work on dynamic wireless power transfer charging systems.

articleTitle: Electrical Simulation Model Identification Method used in Multi-Cell LiFePO4 Battery
abstract: This article provides a method for identifying a single cell electrical simulation model in a multi-cell (12 cell) battery. The battery utilized in this procedure is a set of LiFePO4 cells SP-LFP040AHA. This article describes a single cell SP-LFP040AHA and the infrastructure needed to support it. The board DC2100B, especially the chip LTC6804, was used to detect single cell voltage. Following this step, this paper will evaluate a single cell simulation model created to the PLECS environment. Finally, waveforms of individual cell voltage and total battery voltage are shown below.

articleTitle: Cantilevers for Atomic Force Microscopy Prepared by 3D Laser Lithography
abstract: In this paper, we designed, prepared and characterized new types of IP-Dip polymer based cantilevers for atomic force microscopy (AFM). The design and fabrication is aimed to the capability of 3D laser lithography using standard silicon platform employed in commercial AFM systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Professional Practice in Biomedical Engineering: A Path to Efficient and Innovative Progress
abstract: The article addresses the need for practical experience for students of Biomedical Engineering to enhance the educational process. Practical training was incorporated into the academic curriculum in the 2016/2017 academic year. The text delves into the gradual increase in students' interest in gaining practical experience outside the university environment. It also describes the institutions students choose and where they complete their practical training within Slovakia. Based on this information, a web application was developed where students can access a list of institutions offering practical training opportunities.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Alternative Voltage Type Rectifier for WPT System
abstract: This work focuses on the operational study of wireless power transfer (WPT) systems, with the primary focus being the alternative topology of the secondary side rectifier, for which the system's attributes are being examined. The common choke of the alternative rectifier replaces the two diodes in the bridge rectifier. In order to examine the electrical behavior and determine the most favorable circumstances, also known as terms of efficiency performance at nominal power, a system analysis was first carried out. Consequently, in order to demonstrate the operational behavior in the time domain for each researched rectifier alternative, the findings are compared, analyzed, and then subjected to simulation analysis. Regarding secondary side electrical factors, several correlations have been found, and stress-optimization strategies are also discussed. While individual secondary side rectifier solutions are assessed from an efficiency perspective and recommended operational parameters are followed.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Topologies and the Impacts of Temperature on Their Performance
abstract: This paper analyses the influence of the increased operating temperature on the performances of five PMSM topologies designed with identical general specifications and constraints. The studied topologies are Surface-mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SPMSM), Halbach Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (HPMSM), Inlet Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM), Spoke Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SIPMSM), and V-shape Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (VIPMSM). The electromagnetic torque, back-EMF, and the permanent magnet magnetic flux density are analysed for four operation temperature levels (20°C, 60°C, 100°C, and 140°C). The analysis provides insights on the aspects to be considered for further development of online detecting, locating, and quantifying the degree of PM demagnetisation in PMSM.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Ceramic 3D Printer
abstract: This article deals with the design and control of a ceramic 3D printer. The paper describes the design of the ceramic printer, the development of the extruder and the control of the 3D printer. The paper includes a computer model, analysis and simulation. The aim of the paper is to demonstrate the designed 3D printer and verify its functionality.

articleTitle: Investigating the Motion of a Compound Pendulum Using Video Analysis
abstract: In this paper, we present a modification of the laboratory exercise “Determining the moment of inertia of a compound pendulum” solved by UNIZA students during their studies. The modification consists of shooting a video capturing the movement of the pendulum and its subsequent analysis using the freely available video-analysis tool, Tracker. This analysis allows, except evaluation of the task in a standard way, also the analysis of damped and undamped oscillations of the compound pendulum. The solution to the studied problem thus becomes more complex, gives richer information about the movement of the pendulum, and offers students the opportunity to connect knowledge about the properties of a rigid body performing rotary motion and oscillatory motion, which are usually discussed separately.

articleTitle: Simple Mathematical Model of BESS Suitable for Optimization Purposes
abstract: Modelling of battery systems is becoming an important aspect in the fields of electric power engineering and electromobility. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and optimization algorithms that enable the optimization and efficiency improvement of almost any system, battery models are used as a tool to optimize the operation of electric grids, electric vehicle charging, or storing excess energy generated from renewable sources. Optimization involves a large number of computations with a significant volume of data, so the use of less complex models is advantageous, especially in the initial phases. A simple model can ensure quick calculations, easy supervision, error detection, and the optimization result is more stable and easier to interpret. This article introduces a simple mathematical model of a battery system suitable for the initial stages of optimization problems. The main advantages lie in the straightforward parameterization and implementation of the model.

Author Keywords: Model of Battery Energy Storage System

articleTitle: Design of a Neural Network for Controlling the Output Voltage of a Step-Down DC/DC Converter
abstract: This article deals with the design of an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of mitigating fundamental error mechanisms in power systems, such as step changes in input voltage and load resistance. The primary objective is to create an ANN tailored for a DC/DC buck converter. The exploration includes the selection of an appropriate ANN type and its structural configuration. Additionally, a crucial aspect involves the identification and creation of training input-output datasets, ensuring the ANN effectively serves its purpose. In this context, the aim is to substitute the conventional PID controller with this ANN, tasking it with generating the necessary duty cycle.

articleTitle: Influence of Sensing Contacts on Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Measurement of EV Batteries
abstract: This article deals with the influence of the design of the measuring contact of electrochemical cells on the results measured by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Since battery cells can reach internal series resistance values ​​in the sub milliohm range, impedance measurement becomes a problem. In general, impedance measurement in ranges smaller than 1 mΩ is problematic and makes it difficult to make contacts. Among other things, the EIS method uses injecting of excitation current. Therefore, the measuring contacts' design must have the smallest possible parasitic properties.

articleTitle: Impact of Statistically Small Population Sampling on Threshold Detection
abstract: This paper focuses on statistical sampling technique for the SNR-based threshold detection by using a small population sampling via cell averaging technique applied on a sliding wavelength window. We analyze and also demonstrate the threshold detection capability even with extremely small population sampling. This sampling technique is intended for fiber-optic transmission systems that share fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) sensing applications and telecommunication services in the same single mode fiber (SMF) simultaneously. This is demonstrated on two reference sets of data obtained by using two optical spectrum analyzers (OSA) with sparse and dense population samplings, respectively over the C-band fiber region. It has been shown that an appropriate sizing of statistical sampling has a potential to reduce demands on computational resources.

articleTitle: Thermal Simulation of Second-Life Battery Container Operation
abstract: This study delves into the thermal dynamics of second-life battery containers to analyze their operational parameters including velocity field distribution and temperature gradients. Employing sophisticated computational modeling techniques, the research simulates a standard operational scenario. By scrutinizing factors such as operation periods and internal heat generation, the study accurately captures the complex thermal behavior within these containers. The findings of this research contribute significantly to the advancement of second-life battery technologies, offering a deeper understanding of thermal management strategies. By optimizing thermal performance, these insights facilitate the development of sustainable energy storage solutions, accelerating the transition towards a greener and more resilient energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Silicon Carbide Technology: State-of-the-Art
abstract: This article provides an overview of the most recent developments in silicon carbide research. It provides a brief history of silicon carbide and an overview of devices that use SiC technology today. A short description of the SiC power electronic devices is provided. The article also dives into current trends in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> applications and topologies where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiC}$</tex> power electronics are used. At the end of this article, a quick comparison between classic silicon and modern silicon carbide technology is presented, along with challenges for the future development of the given technology.

articleTitle: Applicability of optical sensors in packaging tasks
abstract: This paper presents a robotic application designed to facilitate sensor collaboration focusing on the detection and verification of correct box closure. The primary objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of integrating BALLUFF's sensors with Mitsubishi's collaborative robot, Melfa ASSISTA. The main purpose of this app is to serve as a role model for expanding collaborative workspaces to improve understanding in robotics, mechatronics, and related fields. The emphasis is on verifying the seamless integration of sensors in the context of a collaborative robotic environment. This plays a key role in supporting the development of knowledge and expertise in the complexly interconnected fields of inquiry, making a significant and notable contribution to the ongoing development and improvement of understanding in these diverse and interrelated fields of study.

articleTitle: A Benchmark Study of Deep Learning Algorithms for PPG Signal Processing
abstract: This study delves into extracting Photoplethysmography (PPG) signals from images using various neural network architectures. The research aims to assess the effectiveness of different models in capturing PPG values from snapshots of the dataset. Two training approaches were investigated: pretraining the model with only the fully connected part being trained or training the entire network. Results demonstrate that the models trained from scratch outperform their pretrained counterparts. Among the architectures, DenseNet121 shows the most promising results. The findings highlight the potential of utilising neural networks for PPG signal extraction, with applications ranging from surgical planning to personalised medical treatments. This research represents a significant stride in integrating advanced imaging techniques and neural networks in biomedical engineering.

articleTitle: Measuring the Polarization State of Light - a Student Lab Exercise
abstract: We design a laboratory exercise for the students of Photonics in the 4th year of their undergraduate studies. The goal is to teach them the concepts of the Stokes parameters that characterize the polarization state of the partially polarized light and the way we can determine them experimentally using a simple polarimeter composed of a quarter waveplate, a linear polarizer and a detector of light.

articleTitle: Investigation On WBG Power Devices Inside Bidirectional PFC in On-Board Charger Applications
abstract: The request of Active Front End (AFE) converters with bidirectional functionality is growing at high rate. This is due to the fast development of smart charging infrastructures related to Car Electrification process and V2G applications inside the Smart Grid. Such power converters are required to provide high performance with high efficiency and overall low complexity. A viable approach to this purpose is the introduction of WBG power devices. In this paper, an overview of active front-end PFC stage for typical 3-phase application is proposed. In particular, a 2-level three-phase full bridge (B6) and a 3-level NPC2 (3L-TType) converters are considered and the opportunity to extend the performance is analyzed. A hybrid WBG implementation, with both SiC and Gan technology are compared in order to highlight the benefits of those technology in 3L-TType configuration.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of Nanocomposite Films Containing WS2
abstract: The study presents the results of research on the electrical properties of nanocomposites containing dichalcogenide in the form of WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (Sample 1) and WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> along with the three-component alloy (Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Zr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>) (Sample 2). The nanocomposites were produced by a dual-source magnetron sputtering method. The electrical properties were examined using impedance spectroscopy. The range of measurement temperatures was from 20 K to 375 K. Samples has been tested in frequency range from 50 Hz to 2 MHz. Conductivity, phase shift angle and frequency factor studies are presented.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Medium- and High-Speed Region
abstract: The research outlines the outcomes of utilizing methods based on a mathematical model of the motor for sensorless control of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) in the medium and high speed range using different strategies, such as Sliding Mode Observer (SMO), Pseudo-Sliding Mode Observer (P-SMO), Luenberger observer (LU) and Luenberger observer in quasi-synchronous γδ frame (LUγδ). The Back-EMF observer utilises stator voltages (u*), stator currents (i), and a mathematical model of the motor. An estimator, like a phaselocked loop (PLL) or an Atan function, is used to determine the rotor speed and position. As the accuracy of these estimates has a direct influence on the quality and dynamics of the sensorless control, precise Back-EMF signal observation is paramount. Additionally, the research exhibits how this was implemented on an actual motor. The results show that the investigated method is able to control the motor at medium and high speed with relatively low deviation between measured and estimated frame. This means that the deviation between the measured and estimated quantities is almost negligible. We conclude that this technique is highly appropriate for controlling the motor at medium and high speeds due to its robustness against parameter changes.

articleTitle: Analysis of losses in ferromagnetic materials in synchronous motor with permanent magnets
abstract: This paper deals with investigation and calculation of iron losses in ferromagnetic materials within different methods with the same material. Laboratory measurements were carried out to calculate the iron losses of an available permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Additionally, the Steinmetz equation was used for analytical calculations of iron losses. Values obtained from Epstein measurements were used for the purpose of calculation and comparison. Lastly finite element analysis was conducted for purpose of iron losses calculation. The outcomes derived from these procedures were then assessed and compared. Refining the calculations of losses gives us a better idea of their origin, behavior, and subsequent reduction, which results in more efficient machines.

articleTitle: Contribution to the Analysis of Digital Infrastructure in Terms of Readiness for Cooperative, Connected and Automated Mobility
abstract: The surge in urban traffic has been linked to various challenges, most notably congestion and accidents-many of which result from human errors, both direct and indirect. CCAM (Connected, Cooperative, Autonomous and Automated Mobility) stands as a potential solution to enhance traffic efficiency, safety, and overall user comfort. Realizing these objectives necessitates the resolution of numerous challenges, such as communication and data processing infrastructure, vehicle technology, protection of personal data, and cybersecurity. This study contributes to the assessment of the readiness of the University of Zilina - Vranie Village route for autonomous transport, focusing on the reliability and speeds of the supporting C- V2X (Cellular vehicle-to-everything), V2I (Vehicle-to-Infrastructure) systems. The results reveal crucial deficiencies in various aspects, necessitating improvements for optimal functionality. While some services meet the requirements at high percentages, significant issues persist, especially in vehicle location accuracy and latency. Notably, non-compliance occurrences suggest inadequacies in the 5G network, emphasizing the need for enhanced network infrastructure. Addressing the deficiencies in network infrastructure, predictive models and stability of the network, while also conducting further research, will be crucial for realizing the potential of autonomous vehicles in both urban and suburban areas.

articleTitle: An Analytical Model of a SiC MOSFETs in Parallel Configuration
abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop an analytical model of a single and two parallel configuration silicon carbide power MOSFETs utilizing the state-space equations to offer a straightforward solution with reduced computational efforts, still maintaining high accuracy. The analytical model of each single power device is directly obtained from technical specifications. Although the main target is to investigate the unbalanced phenomena in paralleled SiC devices, the proposed approach additionally provides a practical model for testing electric drive configurations, control strategies and fault tolerant drives. The analytical model has been validated through simulation implemented in Matlab/Simulink, comparing transient commutation and computational times with SPICE models.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Under Open Phase Condition
abstract: If there is a one-phase interruption anywhere in the distribution network, it results in an asymmetrical power supply of the load. If there are other substations and transformers between the fault and the load, the voltage drop of the affected phase may decrease. This is dangerous for protections because they may not immediately assess the condition correctly. The paper deals with the issue of asymmetrical power supply of induction motors and the effect on their properties, especially warming.

articleTitle: Radon Transform-Based 3D Reconstruction of Brain Vasculature from 2D Angiography
abstract: This study delves into the theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of advanced imaging techniques, specifically focusing on the diagnosis and treatment of brain aneurysms and related vascular pathologies. Beginning with an exploration of the theory behind intracranial aneurysms, we discuss their prevalence, characteristics, and the demographic factors influencing their occurrence. The utilization of diverse diagnostic methods, including CT scans, MRIs, and angiograms, is elucidated for effective aneurysm detection. A critical aspect of this research involves the comprehensive examination of cerebral angiography, a pioneering technique providing detailed images of blood vessels in and around the brain. Originating in 1927, its evolution is traced, highlighting its therapeutic applications and pivotal role in contemporary diagnostic protocols. We explore its superiority over less invasive methods, its role in immediate treatment interventions, and its significance in confirming brain death in certain jurisdictions. The study culminates in an exploration of the historical context of cerebral angiography and its adaptation in the modern era of neuroimaging. While newer technologies have supplanted its role in certain diagnostic scenarios, cerebral angiography persists as an indispensable tool for evaluating various vascular pathologies within the skull. This comprehensive examination sheds light on the intricate interplay between theoretical understanding, diagnostic advance-ments, and therapeutic applications in the domain of neurovas-cular imaging.

articleTitle: Lower Limb Motions Analysis for Development of a Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robotic System
abstract: The aim of this work is the lower limb motion analysis in order to use the results to design an adaptive robotic system for the rehabilitation of lower limbs and to implement adaptive control algorithms. The project aims to obtain an intelligent architecture of the robotic rehabilitation system (3 degrees of freedom) that can perform trajectories similar to a lower limb (hip, ankle, and knee).

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors for Zero- and Low-Speed Region
abstract: The study presents results from the evaluation of sensorless control techniques for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM). The focus is on achieving low mechanical rotor speed using a high frequency (HF) signal injection method and signal demodulation in a dq system. Injecting pulsating voltage into the dq system allows the flux-producing and torque-producing components of the voltage and current to be separated, unlike injecting rotating voltage into the two-phase stationary reference frame αß, which causes increased noise and torque ripple. Utilizing pulsating voltage is more preferable than solely utilizing the d-axis, as it doesn't have as significant an impact on the motor torque. This technique estimates various individual quantities necessary to complete the current transformation between three-phase stationary reference frame abc, two-phase stationary reference frame αß, and rotational reference frame dq, including estimated mechanical rotor speed and estimated electrical rotor position. The study utilises actual measurements and simulations. Additionally, the research exhibits how this was implemented on an actual motor. The results show that the investigated method is able to control the motor at low and zero speed with relatively low amplitude of the injected signal and relatively low saliency of the motor. Conclusion is that this technique is highly appropriate for controlling the motor at low and zero speeds without having a major impact on the torque ripple.

articleTitle: Development of a Smart Non-Lethal Trap Prototype Utilising ESP32-CAM and PIR Sensor
abstract: The increasing global concern regarding humane pest control methods and the need for effective small mammal management in various environments have prompted the development of innovative technologies. This paper presents our ongoing design of a novel smart non-lethal trap prototype for small animals equipped with an ESP32-CAM and PIR sensor. To differentiate between domestic pets and rodents, ResNet50 is utilised and capable of classifying five animals: cats, dogs, martens, rat or mice, and hedgehogs. Traditional rodent control methods often rely on lethal means, which pose ethical and ecological challenges. Most pest control businesses also use the labour-intensive strategy of physically setting up and maintaining rodenticide bait stations on a commercial basis. To address these issues, our prototype leverages the capabilities of the ESP32-CAM to create an intelligent non-lethal trapping solution with the ability to remotely free unwanted captured animals via the cloud.

articleTitle: Design of Educational Model of 8-Bit Serial Communication
abstract: In the article, we proposed a educational model of serial communication, which is adapted to the needs of teaching for the 3rd year of the bachelor's degree in the subject of Design of electronic devices. We have designed a counter with a state machine that controls the counter. We designed and mathematically described an 8-bit serial line transmitter, with a STOP bit. We designed a serial line receiver, and we verified by simulation that the transmitted 8-bit data word is also correctly received. For the serial communication circuit, we have designed a printed circuit board that is adapted for independent operation and also control with a microprocessor.

articleTitle: Biological Influence of Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Field Exposition Based on Selected Cell Death Markers
abstract: This work presents the results of the examination of the HeLa cell line exposure on the ELF-EMF (extremely low-frequency electromagnetic field). In particular, the relationship between ELF-EMF exposition time and cell death. The examination of cell death hallmarks were examined by estimation levels of selected proteins - FACL4 (a protein that is a part of the ferroptosis pathway) and CK18 (Cytokeratin related to necrosis and apoptosis pathways) in the proposed model of workers exposed to ELF-EMF week.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Finite Control Set Model Predictive Direct Speed Control of PMSM
abstract: Finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) stands out as a highly promising and extensively researched control approach due to its exceptional dynamic performance and the versatility it offers for defining control goals. This paper presents a systematic analysis of parameter mismatch and its impact on the control performance of finite control set model predictive direct speed control (FCS-MPDSC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Variations in resistance, inductances, and inertia are studied, and root mean square error (RMSE) metrics are employed to quantify the effects of parameter mismatch on the phase current and angular speed. Results analyze the control performance and provide insights into addressing parameter mismatch challenges in FCS-MPDSC. The predictive control algorithm is designed in dq coordinate system and a linear Kalman filter (LKF) is utilized for the estimation of load torque.

Author Keywords: finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC)

articleTitle: Analysis of the DC-DC Converter Characteristics for Cost Effective Low Voltage Battery Storage System
abstract: This work provides an overview of the basic concept designs for cost effective battery storage system (BSS). The main specific of proposed BSS is utilization of commonly available recycled laptop batteries, while a standard configuration (3S - 3 batteries in series) is considered. Technical solution focuses on the efficiency performance optimization of the system at all. Because of the low level of the ESS voltage and dealing with the efficiency maximization of low-power solar cell, the buck-boost topology is evaluated as a possible solution. Regarding previous mentioned facts, the attention was given on the investigation of the proper control of the converter, while the main aim was to reduce self-consumption of the power circuit, thus increasing system efficiency.

articleTitle: Analytical Comparison of Power Balance Methods for Airgap Torque Accuracy Determination in Automotive Applications
abstract: Information about torque value is critical for today's hybrid electric vehicles and electric vehicles. This information can be used for improving comfort and overall safety of the vehicle. Based on the final torque accuracy of the estimator it is possible to optimize the cost of the whole system. It is unclear how much each component affects the accuracy of the torque estimation. This paper presents the sensitivity analysis of torque calculation utilizing both AC and DC input power and speed of the motor for the calculation. Based on this analysis it is possible to determine which element in the system has the highest impact on the final inaccuracy of the estimator and then modify the subsystems (individual elements) to reach the desired torque accuracy in the most cost-efficient way. The results show that it is possible to use both methods, but the accuracy of the DC power calculation method is better, because of the absence of the position sensor. However, this method requires more computational power because it is necessary to determine the power electronics' losses. Additionally, this method is unsuitable for use in an electric drive system with multiple drive units. Therefore, it is possible to use both methods, because both can be used under different conditions.

articleTitle: Progressive Control Methods of Power Converters: An Overview
abstract: This article focuses on the analysis of progressive control methods employed in power semiconductor converters. These advanced methods primarily aim to enhance regulation properties, particularly in scenarios involving overregulation values or settling times during failure mechanisms. Such failure mechanisms often manifest as step changes in the input voltage of the power converter or variations in the load resistance value. Within this article, we explore three methods: sliding mode control (SMC), model predictive control (MPC), and neural networks (NN). These methods are recognized as progressive methods in the literature, characterized by their improved regulation properties.

articleTitle: What Goes Up……: modelling the Bitcoin rollercoaster ride
abstract: Cryptocurrencies have attracted increasing attention worldwide. Cryptocurrency assets are likely to remain a viable choice for the public in long term. In this paper, the modelling of cryptocurrency price is explored in Bitcoin bubbles prior to and during the COVID-19 pandemic. As shown here, it is necessary and possible to understand the dynamics in plausible proxy variables. A similar methodology could be deployed in other situations where market bubbles occur.

articleTitle: Design and Practical Realisation of a Multichannel Bandpass Filter for the Current DVB-T2 Band
abstract: In the paper, a unique concept of a multichannel Radio Frequency (RF) bandpass filter operating in the current DVB-T2 band is proposed. Based on the analysis of the presented filter concept the prototype was designed and realized. Subsequently, the measurement of the scattering parameters and verification of the filter properties in practical conditions were carried out. The proposed and realised bandpass filter consists of a section for DC signal, two equivalent RF bandpass sections and an additional RF part for improved suppression of unwanted out-of-band signals. In addition to these three basic parts, the structure contains coupling elements that ensure the appropriate connection of individual sections with the elimination of their influence on each other. A prototype of the proposed bandpass filter operating at 533 MHz with a fractional bandwidth of 9.4%, which includes 6 consecutive DVB-T2 channels, is presented.

articleTitle: Iterative Method for Estimating the Parameters of a Linear Transformer Model
abstract: The equivalent circuit of the transformer is an abstract model that describes the real behavior of the transformer. Today, several equivalent circuits are known. The most well-known are the T-equivalent circuit and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi$</tex> -equivalent circuit that derives from it. Parameters are typically estimated by nameplate nominal parameters, short-circuit, open-circuit measurements, etc. In this procedure, the simplifications used introduce inaccuracies into the estimate. This paper describes an iterative method that minimizes inaccuracy.

articleTitle: Simulation of Dual Active Bridge Topology for Second-Life Batteries
abstract: This study designs and validates a bidirectional DC/DC converter via SPICE simulation, connecting a battery and an interconnection circuit with nominal voltages of 120V and 400V, respectively, and a power rating of 5kW using LiFePO4 battery technology. The chosen Dual-active-bridge (DAB) circuit ensures high power density, bidirectional energy flow, and wide soft switching range. Control algorithm design, initially in the analog domain, transitions to digital implementation using bilinear transformation for stability. SPICE simulation verifies theoretical waveforms, quantifies power losses, and validates the control algorithm, with proposed enhancements including a power derating scheme for improved reliability and efficiency under varied operating conditions.

articleTitle: Measurements of the Electric Properties of the Current Collector in a Conductive Electric Road
abstract: Conductive electric road systems are charging in-frastructures that allow electric vehicles to charge while driving. Similar to that of trolleybuses, trams and metro trains conductive electric roads use a physical sliding contact to facilitate the energy transfer between vehicle and road supply. However, as conductive electric roads introduce a new application for the sliding contact, knowledge is scarce on both current collector design as well as the electrical properties of the sliding contact. This paper presents measurements of the currents in the current collector as well as voltage drop and contact resistance across the sliding contact, conducted on an electric road demonstrator. The results reveal the benefits and drawbacks of a current collector design with multiple contacts points as well as provide a range of magnitude in contact resistance for the sliding contact.

articleTitle: Power Inverter Design for Wireless Power Transfer System
abstract: The power inverter design strategy for a wireless power system was provided in this study. Initially, the circuit calculations were presented once the WPT system concept was described. The suggested inverter's operating power levels are close to 25 kW; thus far, the design has taken this power into account. A thorough examination of the power transistor selection was provided since it is a crucial component of the power inverter and, when combined with appropriate driver design, should yield good operational efficiency values. The suggested inverter was built in a lab setting and put through experimental verification. The WPT system, which was set up for certain operating parameters pertaining to the distance between the transmitting and receiving coils, was used to conduct the measurements.

articleTitle: Improving TRISAT-R Satellite Attitude Prediction by Incorporating a High-Resolution Optical Sensor to Kalman Filtering
abstract: When flying a satellite, various operations on-board the satellite require determining quite a precise orientation to properly function, such as Earth or Sun observation, downlink communication and similar. This results in satellite attitude estimation posing a crucial problem to be solved, using a wide array of spacecraft control systems and sensor readings. Due to the noise in magnetic sensor measurements and drift in gyro meters, auxiliary (optical) subsystems are widely used to add reference measurements and correct the noise and the drift. Since the star-trackers, most widely used optical subsystem for attitude estimation, can be relatively large and high energy consuming, a smaller alternative is found in photodiodes and small CMOS cameras, both of which are being currently used on board TRISAT-R. Even with additional optical filters, there is error present in all measurements and error estimation is necessary. Recently the development and use of Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) has shown greater potential for use in space related estimation, due to UKF not using classic Kalman linearization but employing a set of sigma points to calculate the systems mean and covariance more accurately. TRISAT-R use of on-board systems to tackle the problem of attitude estimation is described. UKF filtering is briefly discussed, and the simulation model for UKF of TRISAT-R orbiting is proposed. The results show an increase in accuracy of attitude prediction when using CMOS cameras for prediction instead of photodiodes, which confirms the idea that small cameras can be used for in-orbit photodiode calibration.

articleTitle: Innovation of the Laboratory Exercise for Measurement of Magnetic Field of the Earth
abstract: The instruction of Physics in universities with a technical focus presents distinctive challenges, such as a limited number of Physics sessions per week (comprising 3 lectures, 2 computational exercises, and 1 laboratory session in University of Zilina), diminished student motivation, and a prevalent negative attitude towards Physics. This contribution aims to outline our novel, reformed approach to teaching Physics, with a particular focus on laboratory exercises. It is imperative for students to recognize that Physics serves as the foundational framework for explaining various phenomena that they will encounter in their academic journey. Presently, laboratory exercises in Physics primarily emphasize practical elucidation and comprehension of phenomena through demonstration experiments and subsequent assessments.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Cough Sound Records
abstract: The article deals with the actual R&D problem of detection and analysis of the recording of cough sounds because of mechanical vibrations of the biological structure. It is a reaction of medical practice to the need for qualitative and quantitative evaluation of sounds. The recording of the sounds takes place in the sleep laboratory of the university hospital via polysomnographic ex-amination. The obtained signals are mathematically and statistically evaluated. Wavelet transform, power spectral density, cross-correlation function and other statistically significant parameters are mainly used for the analysis and evaluation of recordings. The obtained results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Computer Modeling of B6-Bridge with EC Motor
abstract: This paper focuses on the computer modeling of a B6-bridge type inverter in conjunction with a BLDC motor in the sense of modeling the entire system which includes the commutation technique, gate driver, inverter and motor. In devolopment, it is very important to have a detailed model of the inverter to deal with transients. In practice, the individual components are supplied by the manufacturers without simulation models and their behavior is unclear, this is the goal of the paper. Furthermore, the simulation of a smart gate driver of a MOSFET transistor is presented in the paper. Another objective of the paper is to develop commutations for BLDC motor control namely trapezoidal and SVPWM commutation. As a result, the paper presents the simulation analysis of the inverter in LTSpice environment for the switching times of the MOSFET transistor and then compares them with real measurements.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 Web Server Performance
abstract: Containerization become a leading trend in the de-ployment of services, especially in cloud environments. There are many container-based virtualization platforms, but Docker is the most popular in the field. In this paper, we present an evaluation that includes important metrics such as requests per second, which measure the average number of requests processed during multiple runs and client scenarios. Additionally, the investigation examines the mean duration of a request and response cycle, as well as the average time required for establishing a connection, including TLS handshake. Moreover, the paper examines the web server's RAM usage under different load conditions. The paper aims to comprehensively understand web server efficiency and responsiveness under low CPU and RAM constraints for both HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 settings through metric analysis.

articleTitle: Topology and Main System Components in Second-Life Battery Energy Storage Systems
abstract: Second-Life Battery Energy Storage Systems (SLBESS) represent a promising direction for optimizing costs in modern smart grids. Although they can help reduce costs, they are highly sensitive components, which places high demands on their design and management. The article focuses on describing the topology and key components for SLBESS. The use of second-life batteries brings economic benefits, but it is necessary to adapt the design of the Battery Energy Storage System. Two product lines of SLBESS with different capacities of 90kW and 150kW are introduced, integrated into standard 20ft shipping containers. The article emphasizes the optimal integration of the entire system to effectively utilize batteries with a second life. In conclusion, measurements of the developed prototype on the AC terminals in grid supply mode are presented.

articleTitle: The Impact of Moisture Diffusion From Paper-Oil Insulation on Oil DC Conductivity
abstract: The paper presents a study of the polarization current of brand-new mineral oil and moistened oil by diffusion from moistened paper-oil insulation with a moisture content of (5 ± 0.2) % by weight. The oil moistening method used in the study enabled the maximal reproduction of phenomena occurring in transformers. Based on the obtained measurement results, the temperature dependencies of the DC conductivity and the activation energy values of the conductivity of the brand-new and moistened oil by diffusion were determined. The obtained measurement results indicate a change in the activation energy of conductivity due to the moistening of the oil, which may significantly affect the accuracy of determining the moisture content of transformer insulation

articleTitle: Noise Analysis of Dry Transformer in the Laboratory Conditions
abstract: The article focuses on the method of assessing the instability of noise and the size of a dry transformer using acoustic emission in laboratory conditions. The experimental measurement was conducted to obtain reference values for the acoustic emission size and its instability of acoustic noise for a well-functioning dry transformer rated at 22000/6000 V in the laboratory. These reference values were then compared with the actual values of the transformer during its operational phase. The measurement utilized a noise measuring device with a three-octave spectral filter, covering the frequency range from 100 Hz to 10 kHz, over a period of 20 seconds. Specifically, a CESVA SC250 measuring device was employed for noise measurement through acoustic emission analysis. It simultaneously measures all parameters, considering both frequency and time parameters across various time bases. These measurements serve as reference values for analyzing the condition of dry transformers of the same type and performance. After operation or repair, transformers can be sent for inspection to test laboratories for comparison and evaluation.

articleTitle: Effect of Power Quality Variations on Electricity Consumption
abstract: In recent years, there has been a degradation in power quality due to the widespread use of modern electronic devices. Office buildings, in particular, employ a variety of devices such as computers and LCD monitors, contributing to a decrease in power factor and an increase in harmonic distortion. This article delves into the investigation of the impact of total harmonic distortion of voltage on power consumption parameters, specifically focusing on two types of computer power sources and LCD monitors. The results demonstrate that diminished power quality leads to an increase in nonactive power and exerts influence on the power factor of commonly used devices in office buildings.

articleTitle: Battery Regeneration with Pulse Charging
abstract: This article presents the possibility of battery regeneration with pulse charging. With pulsing charging is possible to recover the faded capacity of batteries. The result of regeneration is based on how much the structure of the battery is damaged. There are several ways to secure pulse charging like programmable power supply or circuits for shaping and limitation of charging current. In this article, these options are described. One of the key parameters of pulse charging is frequency. The effect of different pulse current frequencies on the same type of battery cell is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Influence of Analog Input Circuits to DSP SAR ADC and its Optimization
abstract: With the growing market and the development of fast digital systems, the requirements for fast sampling of analog quantities also increase at the same time. To increase the speed of the control loops in fast systems, it is necessary to ensure fast sampling. However, this can bring other problems that are not visible at first glance. This paper deals with analysis of the internal circuits of the ADC and influence of this circuits to the external analog devices that are adjusting signals for the ADC such as operational amplifiers in various configurations. Finally, this paper presents guide to proper design input circuits to minimize distortion of the sampled signal by the ADC circuits.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of High-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields in Railway Compartment: A CST Studio Suite Simulation Study
abstract: The influence of radiofrequency (RF) electromagnetic fields (EMF) on human occupants within shielded regions of railway compartment is being investigated in this study using the CST Studio Suite program. The simulations investigate the specific absorption rate (SAR) for 1 gram and 10 grams of human tissue in nine carefully selected settings, with a focus on a Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) operating at 1800 MHz. Within the limited space of the railway wagon compartment, these positions symbolize various spots of the possible human body occurrence. With the 1g method, the highest simulated SAR value was 2.41 W/kg, while with the 10g method, it was 0.98 W/kg.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Based on AC Power Distribution Bus and Matric Converter
abstract: Presented paper discuss feasibility of matrix converter adaptation in dynamic wireless power transfer charging line. The key behaviour of matrix one phase to one phase converter and three phase to one phase converter are presented to get topologies and parameters for adaptation. Get matrix converter features are discussed regarding to the wireless power transfer and dynamic electromobility charging needs. Feasibility of power topology and control approach are discussed as well. Finally, dynamic charging system adapting matrix converter is compared to the conventional topology using active rectifier and inverter in a series. Knowledge taken from the literatures and theoretical discussion is verified by matlab-simulink simulations. At the end, feasibility study decision is done in conclusion.

articleTitle: Charging Power Control Based on Electric Vehicle Owners' Requests for Delivered Energy and Charging Time
abstract: The article is focused on the presentation of the formulation of the control algorithm for managing the charging of electric vehicles while complying with the requirements of the owners of electric vehicles for the resulting state of charge of the battery in a defined time. At the same time, the algorithm maximizes the use of available power from the local photovoltaic source. The functionality of the algorithm is presented through the simulation of a residential charging station's operation.

articleTitle: The Process of Creating an Instructional Video for the Specific Teaching Aids
abstract: Nowadays, modern technologies surround us so much that practically no one can avoid them. Although the use of these modern devices often does not require deep knowledge of their principle and construction, without theoretical knowledge at a certain level, their use is excluded. The rapid obsolescence of technical devices often forces users to study superficially, which can be compensated by searching for various ways of “quick learning” to find effective ways to steepen the learning curve and integrate such methods into the field of education. We can find many examples of supplementary or alternate teaching aids and tools for which there is either an insufficient quantity of appropriate educational content, or even such material is entirely unavailable. The authors describe the possibilities of preparing methodological material, especially for this equipment, focusing on educational video tutorial production. The content of the video tutorials is focused on the uLAB measurement system developed at our department with the perspective of its use in teaching at secondary schools.

articleTitle: Render Performance Optimisation of 3D Application
abstract: In this article, we focused on developing an application to achieve stunning visuals of the digitised campus of the University of Zilina. We discussed various tasks, but our primary focus was on optimisation. We analysed the executed steps that led to the final release version of the 3D application developed in Unreal Engine. Few steps were taken to achieve proper optimization using state-of-the-art techniques. This article discusses the individual stages of development for optimization. The key factor in our optimisation was the use of a plugin that converted dynamic vegetation shadows to static shadows. This preserved the movement of the vegetation, but vastly improved the application's performance. The Shadow Foliage Imposters plugin boosted performance by approximately 52%, compensating for the additional load of dynamic vegetation assets.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Hybrid Energy Storage System Design for Electric Vehicle
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the hybrid energy storage system for electric vehicle is provided. Focus is given on the energy needs of electric vehicle regarding international driving cycle profile. Because combination of supercapacitor and battery provides essential advantages, the evaluation of this alternative is made from the economical point of view.

articleTitle: Control Strategies for Resonance Linear Motor Test Bench
abstract: This paper explores control strategies for resonance linear motor test benches, with a focus on optimizing the response of the system under various conditions. The test bench comprises a linear motor inducing controlled harmonic motion in a slider connected to a spring-fixed system, emulating critical resonance conditions. Additionally, a second linear motor is integrated to impose a controllable load on the slider. The investigation delves into two distinct methods: the Position Synchronized Method and the Force Synchronized Method. The research contributes valuable insights into control strategies for load-emulating linear motors, offering a promising avenue for practical implementation in resonance linear motor test bench. The investigation is exclusively conducted using a simulation model within Matlab Simulink, providing a comprehensive and insightful analysis.

articleTitle: Laboratory Test Bench for Traction Drives with Series-Connected Traction Inverters
abstract: This paper describes development of a test bench of two series-connected traction inverters as hardware-in-the-loop simulator for testing and verification of voltage balancing algorithms. Simulation model is introduced and the results are compared to the test bench results on a test case. Simplified simulation model of a traction drive is used providing sufficient interface to the simulation for two-series connected inverters.

articleTitle: Investigating the Temporal Evolution of the Deformation of Viscous Materials Utilizing Their Birefringence
abstract: In the paper, we analyze the relationship between mechanical deformation and optical birefringence to investigate the possibilities of using birefringence to study the temporal evolution of the deformation of viscous materials. Understanding the connection between the temporal evolution of birefringence and deformation can lead to the development of methods to investigate viscous processes, diffusions, and slow deformations in viscous materials. It also enables the creation of practical non-contact optical deformation, tension/pressure sensors as well as chemical sensors.

articleTitle: Response of Fabry-Perot Interferometric Optical Fiber Sensor to Wheel Defect
abstract: The Fabry-Perot interferometric sensing system can be used not only to determine the speed and number of axles but also, under certain conditions, to determine the technical condition of railway vehicles. The effect of a wheel defect on the track has been replaced by a body with linear momentum to limit the possibility of infrastructure damage. We investigated the influence of the magnitude of momentum and the distance of action from the location of the sensor on the response of the sensor. The findings were applied to a trainset moving at a speed of 98.5 km/h.

articleTitle: Support Element with Magnetic Attachment for Optical Fiber Sensor for Monitoring Railway Traffic
abstract: The article introduces an innovative support element for an optical fiber sensor utilizing a Fabry-Pérot interferometer (FPI) designed for monitoring railway traffic. This removable support element, attached to the bottom of the railway track using permanent magnets, allows for repeated installation and relocation without compromising the sensor's functionality. The support element's metallic structure, magnetic attachment to the rail, and the bonding of the sensing optical fiber ensure adequate protection against environmental conditions. Tested on a railway track for one year, the sensor demonstrated stable positioning and consistent signal detection during the passage of train formations. This design, while tailored for FPI sensors, offers versatile application potential for other optical fiber sensors leveraging fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge Converter With High Efficiency
abstract: The phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) converter is a preferred topology for isolated DC-DC converters with medium to high power levels. It can be utilised in a variety of applications preferably with wide input and/or output range. The efficiency of the converter as well as its power density are important factors for modern applications in the automotive industry or renewable energy sources. New semiconductor components based on gallium-nitride (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaN}$</tex>) and silicon-carbide (SiC) together with suitable converter modification enable to increase in the efficiency and switching frequency. The PSFB converter with controlled rectifier and secondary side energy recovery snubber versa the PSFB converter with synchronous rectifier are compared by simulation for different operational conditions.

articleTitle: Design of an Electrocardiograph with Programmable Signal Gain and Adjustable DRL Circuit Gain – for education purposes
abstract: The aim of this work is to describe the design of a low-cost electrocardiograph with programmable signal gain, which could be used as an educational project for biomedical engineering students. In designing such a device, students will learn to calculate, simulate, and design analog circuit for signal acquisition and preprocessing (filtering noise and amplifying bioelectric signal). They will learn to program a microcontroller (MCU) and use it for digitizing the analog signal, as well as for transmitting data to a computer.

articleTitle: Speech Quality Assessment and Emotions - Effect on the PESQ Metric
abstract: This paper analyzes how emotional speech influ-ences the quality assessment process. The objective metrics for speech quality assessment are usually evaluated with neutral speech recordings, but human interaction frequently involves emotions. Those can modify speech signals' acoustic and phonetic characteristics largely, which are essential from the objective speech quality assessment perspective. The proposed analysis was carried out with the English and Slovenian Interface emotional speech database, which includes two neutral and six emotional speaking styles. Speex codec was used to simulate the degradations, which were then assessed with the lTV - T P.862 PESQ objective metric. The results' analysis showed that in both languages surprise, in English fear, and in Slovenian disgust influenc the speech quality assessment significantly.

articleTitle: Usage of Virtual Instrumentation in Teaching Automotive Buses
abstract: This paper presents the usage of virtual instrumentation as a tool for teaching of automotive bus – CAN BUS. There are multiple applications of virtual instrumentation that leverage the automobile bus to facilitate communication comprehension. The initial method of employing virtual instrumentation involves visualizing the instrument cluster, which is managed by the student's microprocessor-controlled development kit. The demonstrational panel, which includes an accelerator pedal, turbocharger, instrument cluster, and development kit, is also visualized. Using LabVIEW and CAN BUS interfaces, genuine instrument clusters from Skoda and VW automobiles are controlled through the second application of virtual instrumentation. It is simpler for pupils to comprehend the structure of communication through automotive buses of the real vehicle when the instrument cluster is controlled and visualized using the same messages as in the real vehicle.

articleTitle: Design of a Modular Control System for an AGV
abstract: The application of automation technology in logistics aims to enhance efficiency and accelerate the material flow, whether it is from the warehouse to the production station or between multiple workstations in the production process. Automated guided vehicles (AG V s) are generally used to perform these tasks. This paper outlines the development of a software architecture to control AG V s via a programmable logic controller (PLC). The proposed software solution is characterized by a mod-ular structure, facilitating seamless integration and adaptability across various AG V types and their setups. Each functionality of the AG V is addressed through respective software modules, which are located within multiple organizational blocks (cyclic classes), based on the priority of their execution. The suggested software modules are categorized into six groups based on their functions. This article provides a detailed description of the “Platform/Chassis” group, focusing on the movement of the AG V.

articleTitle: DC Conductivity of Electrical Pressboard Impregnated with Mineral Oil of Natural Origin at Various Moisture Levels
abstract: The paper details the findings from an investigation into polarization currents and direct current conductivity of electrical pressboard manufactured by Weidman. The pressboard exhibited moisture levels ranging from 1% to 6% by weight and was impregnated with NYNAS NYTRO BIO 300X, an insulation oil sourced from natural origins. The study involved analyzing how polarization currents and DC conductivity varied with time across measurement temperatures spanning from 20 °C to 70 °C. An Arrhenius plot was crafted, encompassing six temperatures across the entire measurement spectrum. Linear approximations were applied to the experimental data on the Arrhenius plot. From these plots, the activation energy of DC conductivity, determination coefficient (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) values, and standard deviation were determined. The determination coefficient values nearing unity underscore the precision of the measurements and the consistency of temperature conditions. Notably, the study revealed an activation energy value of ΔW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σDC</inf> = 1.069 eV for the DC conductivity of pressboard impregnated with NYNAS NYTRO BIO 300X, a bio-oil of natural origin. (Abstract)

articleTitle: EEG Signals Preprocessing for BCI Systems Using Visual Evoked Potentials
abstract: In this work, we focus on brain stimulation using the VEP (Visual Evoked Potentials) principle. The brain is stimulated by stimulating videos that contain different categories of animals. By stimulating, we generate an electrical signal that we can measure with an EEG device. We selected the Ultracortex Mark IV, which is affordable for relatively good sensing quality. The acquired signal is further processed - we remove the DC offset from the signal using Fourier transform and then filter the signal with a high-pass and low-pass filter. In the first scenario, we try to see if similar or identical signals are emitted from the brain when different people are stimulated by the same video. The second scenario investigates whether one person can recognize different categories of animals. The similarity of the signals was detected by means of correlation coefficients. This would confirm the correctness of the visual stimulations, and we could create a system for non-verbal human-machine communication.

articleTitle: Assessing Biological Responses of Saccharomyces Cerevisiae to Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields: Insights and Implications
abstract: This study investigates the biological effects of Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields (LF-EMF) on Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast cells, an essential model organism in biological research. To achieve controlled exposure, the exposure system ensuring uniform exposition while maintaining identical cultivation conditions for both exposed and control samples is used. To evaluate the impact of LF-EMF, yeast cell growth and proliferation were quantified using a Bürker chamber before and after exposure. Our findings reveal statistically significant differences between the exposed and control samples, suggesting a potential biological response to LF-EMF. The present research offers valuable insights into the effects of LF-EMF on biological cells, contributing to the broader understanding of electromagnetic field's impact on living organisms. Furthermore, the proposed exposure system provides a reliable platform for future bioelectromagnetic research, facilitating health risk assessments and investigations into the therapeutic potential of LF-EMF exposure.

articleTitle: Contactless Diagnostics of Dry Transformers During Operation Condition
abstract: The examination of the increasing noise in the distribution transformer station next to the offices is the focus of this paper. Office workers' mental health has been found to be disturbed by some features of transformer noise at tone frequencies about 400 Hz, even if the standard for noise exposure in the workplace is satisfactory. The noise analysis is focused on acoustic measurements carried out on two 22/0.4kV power dry transformers with the same performance, while one of them, referred to as “noisier”, negatively affects the working well-being of employees. During the acoustic analysis, a parabolic camera was used to identify the cause of the increased noise from the exposed transformer. This procedure makes it possible to analyze the frequency spectrum with the possibility of 3D observation of the dry transformer and to determine the displayed point with the highest noise and acoustic emission. The analysis was carried out during the operation of only one power transformer under no-load conditions and under real load in order to avoid the mutual influence of emission interference.

articleTitle: Design of Educational Model of 4-Bit Multiplier
abstract: In the paper we design of the teaching model of the 4-bit multiplier. In the beginning of paper, we will show how to create a mathematical model of a full adder, which is necessary for the operation of the multiplier. We will represent the basic model of the full adder and more reliable version of full adder. We will compare the reliability of the individual logic elements from which is the full adder made and subsequently show how to create a n-bit full adder. Using an example, we will show how to multiply two binary numbers and based on the solution procedure of the example, we will propose a logical model of a 4-bit multiplier. Finally, we measure propagation delays on the physical model of a 4-bit multiplier.

articleTitle: BMS Battery Unit Architecture for Second-Life Batteries
abstract: Second-life batteries are battery cells obtained from electric vehicles where their capacity is no longer sufficient. One option for recycling is their second use in stationary energy storage systems. Second-life battery cells require a specialized approach to their management in energy storage systems. Firstly, significant differences between various cells arising from uneven wear must be effectively compensated for. Additionally, the battery management unit of the battery management system must implement additional functionalities required of such a system. One of the important functions is efficient and reliable thermal management of the connected batteries.

articleTitle: Introduction to the Issue of the Use of Voltage and Current Pulses in the Electrolytic Production of Hydrogen
abstract: This article discusses the importance and potential of pulsed electrolysis as a method of hydrogen generation with an emphasis on optimizing the efficiency of the process. It focuses on comparing the use of pulsed current and voltage versus DC current, emphasizing the influence of various parameters and their role in increasing the efficiency of the electrolytic process. It discusses the results of an experimental analysis that compares the efficiency of different modes of pulsed electrolysis against DC current. At the same time, it emphasizes the significant influence of parameters such as frequency, voltage and electrode material on the efficiency of the process. The article also provides recommendations for further research in the area of increasing the efficiency of pulsed electrolysis, which could lead to a significant shift in the field of hydrogen energy production.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Used in Technical Diagnostics and Maintenance
abstract: Integrating digital data and human sensory input in real-world settings offers new possibilities in device diagnostics and maintenance. In this study, we utilized the EcoStruxure Augmented Operator Advisor to develop an augmented reality application for a family house heating system. Our application was designed without access to the real heating system; instead, we simulated its operation with a programmable logic controller. Our final application includes three primary scenes: the heat pump, its indoor unit, and the engine room. Drawing on our practical experience, we discuss the benefits of our approach and the software tools used and summarize our subjective opinions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emergency Response: The Leg-Pulling Robot for Efficient Evacuations
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration into the critical aspect of effector design within the context of mobile platforms utilised during emergency scenarios. In times of crisis, ranging from natural disasters to man-made incidents, the efficiency and versatility of mobile platforms equipped with specialised effectors play a pivotal role in ensuring effective response and mitigation. The proposed robotic system consists of a universal platform, a robotic arm, and a custom effector with controls. Our experimental verification of the system shows promising results and the feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Tunable Laser Interference Lithography for Extreme Period Range Gratings
abstract: We introduce a method called period mixing for fabricating diffraction gratings with an extreme range of periods. This method uses capability of laser interference lithography to easily aggregate multiple optical fields. Period mixing principle is described to obtain relations for the interference field characterization. Incorporating motorized components into this optical system has opened new possibilities for fine period tuning, enhancing the precision and efficiency of the process. Gratings featuring different aspects of period mixing are both designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: DC/DC Converter Architecture for Use of Second-Life Batteries
abstract: This scientific article focuses on the architecture of DC/DC converters for the utilization of second-life batteries. The introduction provides general information on the topic. It then addresses two main methods of arranging DC/DC converters: series and parallel. Each section discusses the advantages, challenges, and technical aspects of the respective approach. Subsequently, significant topologies of bidirectional converters, such as the Dual Active Bridge (DAB) and non-isolated buck-boost converter, are described and discussed. These topologies offer high efficiency and flexibility but are associated with certain technical challenges, such as manufacturing and maintenance requirements. Another section delves into a specific architecture of a DC/DC converter characterized by high efficiency due to soft switching of power transistors. The choice of transformer winding ratio and the size of the working inductor are also discussed, with an emphasis on maximizing efficiency and minimizing losses. Overall, the article provides a comprehensive view of the architecture of DC/DC converters for the utilization of second-life batteries and examines various aspects influencing their efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Finite Element Method of the System for Measuring the Magnetization Characteristics of MR Fluids
abstract: In the automation and robotics industry, there is an increasing interest in the magnetization properties of intelligent materials, such as magnetorheological fluids (MR fluids). The article discusses the method of obtaining the magnetization characteristics of MR fluids and compares them with the results of finite element analysis. The use of MR fluids was also discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Efficiency Performance of 3-Phase and 6-Phase Voltage Source Inverter
abstract: Potential future trends led to the automobile industry's proposal for six-phase powertrains. Due to this fact, the article deals with the power analysis, which is devoted to topologies, used within powertrain of the vehicle, i.e. Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) topology in standard 3-phase and extended 6-phase configuration. The simulation program PLECS analyzes topologies, calculates the power losses of semiconductor devices, and processes the data gathered from each investigated topology. The goal of the power parameter analysis is to determine which of the topologies, given the identical input parameters, results in the inverter system's maximum efficiency at different power levels.

articleTitle: Choosing Right Topology for Bidirectional Power Converter Used in a Battery Storage System Based on Efficiency and Economic Perspective
abstract: This paper deals with the topology selection for the DC-DC section of a power converter, which is part of a battery energy storage system. In evaluating the topology options, economic indicators for the actual production of the device as well as for the costs associated with continuous operation were evaluated. The comparison focuses on two competing topologies that allow bidirectional power transfer with an identical number of switching elements.

articleTitle: Influence of Slot/Pole Combinations on the Performance of Dual-Rotor Axial-Flux Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Electric Motor for Automotive Applications
abstract: In this paper, the authors present a comparison between different structures of axial flow electrical machines - dual rotor - surface mounted permanent magnets - yokeless stator and concentric winding. The comparison is made with iso-geometric dimensions (size and weight) and iso-electrical parameters (current and supply voltage) between different slots / poles combinations. The main objective is to classify these structures according to the torque density. A second classification based on electromagnetic performance (losses, power factor, demagnetization risk) is also performed, considering the specification of medium-size electric car. The study is performed using 3D-FEA calculations for better accuracy of the results.

Author Keywords: axial flux permanent magnet electric motor

articleTitle: Analytical Evaluation and Experimental Study of the Developed Web-Application - Space Information Systems and Technologies - for Student Training and Control in English Language
abstract: The relevance of the chosen topic lies in the fact that the development of an information system for teaching and controlling students in English in the training program “Informatics and Computer Science” can compete with other analogues. The developed web application corresponds to educational tasks and its content depends on the necessary needs of technical university students. This will help to improve the quality of the pedagogical process at the university, simplify and facilitate it both on the part of teachers and students, thereby reducing the teachers’ burden of the discipline “Foreign Language” and increasing the assimilation of this discipline by students based on their interest. Currently, more and more attention is paid to E-learning and distance technologies, which are actively used in the university both independently and mixed with a blended type of education. The systems of learning management are considered, their similarities and differences are presented. The examples are given describing the most popular LMS systems today. An analytical evaluation of the developed information system for teaching and controlling students in English in the training program “Informatics and Computer Science” was carried out, which was realized with respect to four existing distance learning systems, namely: MOODLE, Claroline, Atutor and OpenACS. The main criteria by which the experimental study was carried out were determined, the advantages and disadvantages were identified.

articleTitle: Application of the State Space Method in the Solution of Power Semiconductor Converters
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of state space analysis as an analytical approach in addressing challenges within the domain of power semiconductor converters. The application of this method was a pivotal component of the Power Semiconductor Systems course, where students were tasked with the comprehensive analysis of fundamental power semiconductor systems.
