Specifically, this analysis encompassed the examination of essential converter topologies, including rectifiers, DC/DC converters, and inverters. In the course of their studies, students harnessed their proficiency in mathematics, power electronics, and power semiconductor converters to construct comprehensive mathematical models of these converters. Subsequently, they leveraged the versatile capabilities of the Matlab programming environment to execute simulations of these converters. This mul- tifaceted approach not only served to substantiate the method's efficacy but also functioned as a validation of the students' knowledge and understanding of this critical field.

articleTitle: Implementation of Laboratory Exercises in the Process of Teaching the Subject of Electrical Circuits
abstract: Any study program established on Electrical Engineering must include Electrical Circuit Theory. A well-written practical guide supplemented by practical exercises fills in the gaps between theory and practice for students. This article deals with implementing laboratory exercises on the subject of Electrical Circuits for students in the 1st year of their bachelor's degree at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology. The article describes the teaching practice in these newly introduced laboratory exercises. The history of teaching the subject in faculty is long. Over the years, it has undergone many changes. Electrical circuits are a critical profile subject at the faculty level, and it is a fundamental element of many subsequent courses. The subject is taught in the winter semester of the first year of bachelor's studies. We analyse the new teaching process after the new accreditation, as well as experiences with laboratory exercises and feedback from students after the first semester of teaching the subject, representing the basis of the knowledge portfolio of FEIT UNIZA students. The attractiveness of laboratory exercises in the subject for students is ensured by the new equipment of the laboratory and the creation of new tasks.

articleTitle: Control Strategies for Electric Vehicle Drives: FOC Implementation with MTPA and Field Weakening
abstract: The reliability and performance of Electric vehicles (EVs) rely on effective control of electric drives, thereby improving the overall driving experience. To efficiently control the electric drive, this paper implemented a Field Oriented Control (FOC) scheme for controlling a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive designed for EVs. The FOC scheme is integrated with Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) and field weakening control strategies to broaden the speed range of the drive at rated power density and maximum torque. The entire FOC control scheme and MTPA control reference function block are modeled using MATLAB/SIMULINK. The paper comprehensively reviews the mathematical equations governing FOC, field weakening control, and MTPA methods. The research also incorporates simulation results obtained under various driving conditions for EVs, demonstrating the effectiveness of the implemented control strategies.

articleTitle: BMS Controller Architecture for Second-Life Batteries
abstract: As electromobility progresses, there is a growing production of batteries that will eventually require recycling. One potential approach to recycling involves repurposing worn yet still functional batteries into energy storage systems, providing them with renewed functionality. Every battery assembly requires a Battery Management System (BMS), which ensures proper and safe functionality. In the case of recycled cells, the BMS system becomes more intricate due to significant disparities in wear and subsequent parameters among the cells. Second-life batteries extracted from electric vehicles may exhibit various parameters across a single battery pack due to manufacturing tolerances and uneven usage during operation in an electric vehicle. In practice, when using second-life batteries, modules from different electric vehicles of the same model designation are typically utilized. However, if advantageous, modules of different types can also be combined. These facts establish the requirement for a highly universal modular system, which by its nature can cover a wide range of applications of modules of different types and stages of wear. The mentioned module provides a solution to this type of complex problems that cannot be addressed by conventional commercially available products. This paper aims to present the architecture concept and design of the key parts of a universal and flexible BMS control module created based on the requirements arising from the analysis of extended types of second-life battery modules in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Multimodal Analysis of Tissue Dynamics - Spotlight on Perfusion and Temperature
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a multimodal system for the noninvasive assessment of tissue perfusion. The system comprises two measurement modalities: photoplethysmography imaging (PPGI) and infrared thermography imaging (IRTI). Both methods provide crucial information about the tissue's condition; one in terms of blood perfusion and the other in terms of the skin tissue temperature. The dynamics of changes in these parameters induced by external stimuli could offer more insights into comprehending the interdependence of physiological responses. In the scope of this paper, an experiment involving the application of a vasodilating cream to the skin was conducted. Subsequently, we utilized the proposed measurement setup to monitor changes in tissue parameters. The results of the study demonstrate an increase in temperature and perfusion of the tissue to which the vasodilator cream was applied. The data also suggest different dynamics of the sensed parameters.

articleTitle: The Influence of Electromagnetic Field on Honey Bee Workers – Review Paper
abstract: The environment in which insects live, especially honey bees, which are natural pollinators, is increasingly polluted by electromagnetic fields. The impact of the anthropogenic electromagnetic field on bees depends on its frequency and intensity. A wide range of these variables have different effects on bees. This is manifested by changes in physiology, different behaviors and energy absorption by the bee's body. The article reviews these effects in relation to: low-frequency electric fields at a frequency of 50 Hz, electromagnetic fields generated by mobile telecommunications networks and high-frequency electric fields (2 ÷ 240) GHz. Most studies reported an adverse effect of the field on honey bee colony populations. Additionally, a method of protecting bees and hives against infection using an electromagnetic field, i.e. ultraviolet UV-C radiation, was presented. The paper presents a synthetic assessment of the impact of the electromagnetic field on honey bee workers based on a literature review.

articleTitle: Methodological Basics of Digital Technologies in the Innovative Education System
abstract: The article examines the concept content of innovative education, education digitalization and digital technologies. Based on the source analysis, distance education and distance technologies are described as an integral part of digital technologies. The experience of technical universities using digital technologies is presented.

articleTitle: A Minimal-Resource LDPC Encoder and Decoder Design for Memory-Constrained Systems
abstract: In this paper we present our LDPC encoder and decoder design focused on, but not limited to, the LDPC codes described in the recent CCSDS space data systems standard, known as the Blue Book. Two important code transformations: shortening and puncturing are described in detail with the goal of introducing a wider range of LDPC code parameters for Adaptive Coding and Modulation and minimizing the transceivers memory requirements. The effects of these transformations on the error performance of the system are evaluated using Monte-Carlo simulations and a provided along with the newly added LDPC code parameters set and memory-constraints analysis. Our custom free and open-source C implementation of both encoder and decoder is provided along with supporting MATLAB mini-toolkit for LDPC code lifting and transformations. This toolkit further includes also a full implementation and transformations of the QC-LDPC codes utilized in the Wi-Fi 6 IEEE 802.11ax standard.

articleTitle: Renewable Sources – A Genetic Perspective and Application Architecture for Improved Underwater Astronomy Observations
abstract: The conduct of underwater astronomy is an important scientific investigation and procedure. Underwater astronomy observations require the provisioning of power to operate underwater telescopes. The observation should be done while enhancing the angular resolution and not constituting an extra load on the grid. Underwater astronomy uses underwater telescopes that are needed to ubiquitously detect neutrinos. The research proposes a novel light interception approach for the generation of electricity in the deep underwater environment. The proposed energy utilizes bio-engineered bioluminescence to realize electrical energy for underwater telescope operation. The use of the proposed energy source enables underwater telescopes to be located at different underwater locations with significant capacity to enhance the baseline. The use of the proposed approach for powering underwater telescopes enhances the observation i.e., angular resolution by an average of (34.8 – 47.8)%.

articleTitle: Combining RFID and Image-Based Vehicle Identification Data to Detect Illegal Vehicles
abstract: Effective Road law enforcement is a vital part of transportation systems. Escalating traffic congestion and widespread illegal road usage pose fresh hurdles for road law enforcement systems. An intelligent system that aims to reduce illegal road use must enable immediate intervention on a tactical level without disrupting the flow of legal vehicles. To achieve a fast tactical response, strategic-level information, such as location and identity, must ensure law enforcement officials are in the right place at the right time. This paper presents a system that equips authorities with the correct information to act against illegal road users while maintaining normal traffic flow. The proposed system improves upon existing solutions by combining Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) and Computer Vision (CV) data to detect and identify illegal vehicles. The authorities can leverage this information to remove illegal vehicles from the road without affecting the legal road user's experience. This paper is the first to quantify the performance of this concept based on real-world performance criteria through practical experiments. Our work verifies that the theoretical requirements to read a combination of data fields that enable accurate vehicle identification of vehicles traveling at high speeds can be achieved in practice for various scenarios.

articleTitle: Coherent Pluggable Optical Transceivers: Performance Versus Interoperability
abstract: Coherent optical transceiver evolution has been the major driver for the cost-effective increase of capacity in optical networks, enabling ever higher traffic volumes across metro, regional, long-haul and submarine networks. Traditionally, these devices have been proprietary and embedded in dedicated line cards, which are deployed and managed within the transport network domain. With the emergence of implementation and multi-source agreements for coherent optical transceivers in pluggable form factors, savings in cost, power consumption and footprint can now be realized. Furthermore, by installing these transceivers directly in routers/switches the long-envisioned IP-over-DWDM architecture becomes possible. Nevertheless, extending the benefits of coherent pluggable transceivers to network segments that have stringent performance requirements, such as regional and long-haul networks, is challenging. This paper compares the deployment in a reference regional network of coherent pluggable transceivers that retain interoperability (at the expense of limited performance) and proprietary coherent pluggable transceivers designed for best-in-class performance. Simulation results show that the latter allow to increase usable network capacity while also using fewer transceivers, suggesting they are likely more suitable to address the demanding regional and long-haul network segments.

articleTitle: Misuse of Wi-Fi Data to Analyze User Behaviour
abstract: There has been a huge increase in the number of mobile devices over the past few years. Many mobile users own more than one mobile device. Compared to conventional laptops, mobile devices are constantly active and their users use them outdoors more often than personal computers. Compared to desktop computers, mobile devices accompany their owners on their travels and therefore there is a significant risk of tracking and eavesdropping on user data without a user being aware of it. This paper describes techniques how the attacker could track users by using the Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) network. Every mobile device generates traffic that can be divided into “Automatic” and “User”. When” Automatic” traffic is generated, the device can be found because of its pattern. The paper also describes how the attacker can get into the victim's Wi-Fi network without being in its range. When breaching the Wi-Fi network security, the attacker can connect to the victim's network during his first appearance in range of this network. Security pre-cautions and possible directions of future work are discussed at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Design of a Modular GaN-Based Three-Phase and Three-Level ANPC Inverter
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 800 V 11 kVA three-level three-phase active neutral point clamped inverter, utilizing 650 V gallium nitride enhancement-mode high-electron-mobility transistors. The proposed scaled-down prototype design will be evaluated in electric traction systems. The modular approach of the presented power converter design is detailed discussed and the different parts composing the power converter are presented, together with critical design issues. In particular, the design addresses the gate driver design, as well as technical issues related to the thermal analysis, dc current density and parasitics extraction.

articleTitle: The Concept of a Universal Measuring System of Physical Quantities
abstract: In this paper, the issue of integrating several technologies and approaches used in measuring physical quantities is processed. Besides this, the contribution also covers the obtained data's basic processing, conversion, and storage. Emphasis is placed on low-cost solutions oriented to simplicity of construction and intuitive control, suitable for deployment in education.

articleTitle: The Supplementary Education of Physics for Incoming STEM Students - Force Concept Inventory During Years 2020-2022
abstract: This article highlights the role of supplementary education for incoming university students, particularly those entering their first year. Over the past eight years, our university has observed significant gaps in the foundational knowledge of mathematics and physics among new students. To address this issue, we introduced preparatory courses in Mathematics and Physics before the start of the academic year. These courses, initially offered to students voluntarily, aim to fill knowledge gaps and enhance students' understanding. The preparatory courses are open to students from any faculty at the University of Žilina (UNIZA). The Physics course covered essential topics such as physics units, kinematics, dynamics, gravity, and molecular physics, with twenty lessons per week. From 2016 to 2022, we consistently evaluated students' physics knowledge before and after the preparatory course using the standardized Force Concept Inventory (FCI) test. The results indicate that participating in the Summer Course in Physics before the winter semester significantly contributes to students' success in their university studies.
